items.title: Jones Hank — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Earl Garner told me something, we were riding downtown on the subway one day. ... That tells me that, yes, you don't have to play every note on the piano every time you sit down. ... I think that sort of altered my thinking, my musical thinking, a lot of that time.

ctx.x: Good morning! Unknown: We have a beautiful day.

Yes. But, when you're playing solo, then you remember all the things that he couldn't do when you are accompanying. Now, sometimes you can incorporate some of those things into your playing. Still, you have to learn what not to do. Earl Garner told me something, we were riding downtown on the subway one day. Of course, I used to ask him questions, "How do you play this?" He told me something I have never forgotten. I thought it was particularly relevant coming from him because he plays a great style. He said it…
Do you think that’s a lesson that the current generation of "virtuosos" need to learn?
